subject: accountancy
chapter_title: Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm - Admission of a Partner

concepts.title: New Profit Sharing Ratio
concepts.definition: Once an incoming partner takes a slice of profit, every old partner's slice shrinks; the full set of revised fractions for all partners together forms the new profit sharing ratio.
concepts.key_idea: Profit shares always total one, so whatever the entrant gains must come out of the existing partners' portions.
question_patterns: find the new profit sharing ratio when a partner is admitted
calculate the new ratio of all partners after the admission
what is the new profit sharing ratio among the old partners and the incoming partner
determine the ratio in which A, B and C will share future profits after C joins
in Class 12 partnership accounts, work out the revised profit sharing proportion on admission
state the profit ratio of the reconstituted firm once the entrant takes a stated share

solution_steps.action: write each share as a fraction of the whole
solution_steps.explain: convert every partner's entitlement, old and new, into fractions that can sit on one denominator
deduct the exact part surrendered, or scale the old fraction by the profit left once the entrant's part is set aside
express all revised fractions over one common denominator; the numerators read out as the new ratio

concepts.title: Remaining Share Method for an Old Partner
concepts.definition: When the deed is silent about whose shares the entrant buys into, the profit left after the entrant's slice is shared by the old partners in their old proportion; one partner's revised entitlement is his old fraction times that leftover.
concepts.key_idea: Silence about the source of the entrant's share means the old ratio keeps applying to whatever profit remains.
question_patterns: find the old partner's new share under the remaining share method
calculate A's share when C is admitted for a fraction and no sacrifice detail is given
what fraction of profit will an old partner hold after the new partner enters
determine the continuing partner's revised share assuming sacrifice in the old ratio
compute each old partner's slice of the profit left after the incoming partner's share
how much of the profit does an existing partner keep once the entrant takes his part

solution_steps.action: take away the entrant's slice from the whole
solution_steps.explain: the profit left for the old partners is one minus the incoming share

solution_steps.action: scale the old fraction by the leftover
solution_steps.explain: the old partner keeps his old proportion of whatever profit remains

concepts.title: New Share After a Fixed Surrender
concepts.definition: If the admission terms name the exact fraction an existing partner gives up, that partner's revised entitlement is just his old fraction reduced by the surrendered piece.
concepts.key_idea: Add up every surrendered piece and the total equals the entrant's share.
question_patterns: find the new share of a partner who surrendered a stated fraction
calculate the share left after giving part of it to the new partner
what does a partner hold once he has surrendered a named portion
deduct the surrendered fraction from the old share to get the revised share
work out the revised entitlement of each partner after fixed surrenders
how much profit share remains with a partner who gave away a quoted piece

solution_steps.action: subtract the surrender from the old fraction
solution_steps.explain: the difference is what the partner still owns of the profit

concepts.title: Sacrifice Share of a Partner
concepts.definition: For any continuing partner, the piece of profit handed to the entrant equals the share held before admission minus the share held afterwards.
concepts.key_idea: A minus result flips the meaning: that partner gained share instead of giving it up.
question_patterns: how much share has the old partner sacrificed
calculate the sacrifice made by a partner on admission of a new partner
find the portion of profit given up by an old partner
what is the extent of sacrifice when both the old and the new share are known
measure the reduction in a partner's profit share after the admission
compute the loss of share suffered by each existing partner

solution_steps.action: deduct the new fraction from the old fraction
solution_steps.explain: the difference measures exactly how much profit share moved to the entrant

concepts.title: Sacrificing Ratio
concepts.definition: Setting each old partner's sacrifice side by side gives the sacrificing ratio, the proportion in which the goodwill premium is handed over to them.
concepts.key_idea: The sacrificing ratio compares how much share each old partner gives up; premium money follows it.
question_patterns: calculate the sacrificing ratio of the old partners
find in what ratio the existing partners sacrificed their profit shares
what is the ratio in which the goodwill premium will be divided
determine the sacrificing proportion when the new ratio is given
calculate the sacrificing ratio when the new profit sharing ratio is given
work out how the premium is split between the sacrificing partners
compare the sacrifices of the old partners to get their ratio
what is the sacrificing ratio of A and B on the admission of C

solution_steps.action: list old and new fractions for each old partner
solution_steps.explain: both shares must sit on a common denominator before comparing

solution_steps.action: subtract new from old for every old partner
solution_steps.explain: each difference is that partner's sacrifice

solution_steps.action: reduce the differences to whole numbers
solution_steps.explain: the simplified pair or triple of differences is the sacrificing ratio

concepts.title: Goodwill by Average Profits Method
concepts.definition: The firm's past profits are averaged over the agreed span, and that average multiplied by the agreed years' purchase is taken as the goodwill.
concepts.key_idea: A steady profit history stands in for the earnings a fresh business would miss in its first years.
question_patterns: calculate goodwill at a given number of years purchase of average profits
value the goodwill of the firm on the average profits basis
find goodwill using the simple average profits method
what is the goodwill if the average profit and the years purchase are known
determine the value of goodwill from the profits of the last few years
compute goodwill when past profits are averaged and multiplied by the purchase years

solution_steps.explain: divide the total profit of the reviewed years by the number of years
goodwill equals the average profit times the agreed purchase multiplier

concepts.title: Goodwill by Weighted Average Profits
concepts.definition: Recent years get larger weights, and goodwill is valued by applying the purchase multiplier to the weighted average rather than the plain average.
concepts.key_idea: Weights tilt the average toward recent performance when profits show a rising or falling trend.
question_patterns: calculate goodwill on the basis of weighted average profits
value goodwill when weights are attached to each year's profit
find goodwill using the weighted average with weights one two three four
what is the goodwill at given years purchase of the weighted average profit
determine goodwill after weighting the recent profits more heavily

solution_steps.explain: multiply every profit by its weight and total the products
add the weights attached to the years

solution_steps.action: divide the products by the weights
solution_steps.explain: the quotient is the weighted average profit
goodwill equals the weighted average profit times the years purchase

concepts.title: Goodwill by Super Profits Method
concepts.definition: Only earnings above the normal return on capital employed count: deduct the normal profit from the average profit, then multiply the excess by the agreed years' purchase.
concepts.key_idea: Goodwill exists only where the firm beats the normal rate of return on its capital.
question_patterns: calculate goodwill by the super profits method
value goodwill at given years purchase of the super profit
find the super profit and then the goodwill of the firm
what is the goodwill when the normal profit is deducted from the average profit
determine goodwill from the excess earnings over the normal return on capital

solution_steps.explain: capital employed times the normal rate of return over one hundred
average profit less normal profit gives the excess earning
goodwill is the super profit times the agreed purchase multiplier

concepts.title: Goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profits
concepts.definition: Capitalise the average profit at the normal rate to get the implied worth of the business, then subtract the actual net assets; the gap is the goodwill.
concepts.key_idea: Goodwill is whatever the capitalized earnings exceed the tangible worth of the business.
question_patterns: calculate goodwill by capitalisation of average profits
value goodwill after capitalising the average profit at the normal rate
find goodwill as the capitalised value of profits less net assets
what is the goodwill when the capitalized profits exceed the net assets
determine goodwill under the capitalisation method from average profits and net assets

solution_steps.explain: multiply the average profit by one hundred and divide by the normal rate
goodwill is the capitalized value minus the actual capital employed

concepts.title: Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profits
concepts.definition: The excess earning itself is capitalized at the normal rate of return, which gives goodwill straight away without valuing the whole business.
concepts.key_idea: This lands on the same figure as capitalising average profits when both start from the same data.
question_patterns: calculate goodwill by capitalising the super profits
value goodwill as the capitalised value of the super profit
find goodwill when super profits are capitalized at the normal rate
what is the goodwill under the capitalisation of super profits method
determine goodwill by capitalizing the excess earnings at the normal rate of return

solution_steps.explain: capital employed times the normal rate over one hundred
average profit less normal profit
multiply the super profit by one hundred over the normal rate

concepts.title: Premium for Goodwill of the Incoming Partner
concepts.definition: The entrant compensates the old partners by paying for his own slice of the firm's goodwill; that premium equals the firm goodwill times the profit fraction he acquires.
concepts.key_idea: The premium is then shared by the old partners in their sacrificing ratio.
question_patterns: calculate the premium for goodwill brought in by the new partner
how much goodwill premium will the incoming partner pay
find the new partner's share of the firm's goodwill
what amount of premium is due from a partner admitted for a given share
compute the goodwill share the entrant must bring in cash

solution_steps.action: apply the acquired fraction to the firm goodwill
solution_steps.explain: the entrant pays for his slice of the reputation value

concepts.title: Hidden Goodwill
concepts.definition: When goodwill is not quoted, infer it: gross up the entrant's payment to the whole-firm capital, subtract the capital actually standing, and the difference is the hidden goodwill.
concepts.key_idea: The unquoted value is read off from how much capital the entrant paid for his fraction.
question_patterns: calculate the hidden goodwill of the firm
find goodwill when its value is not given at the time of admission
what is the inferred goodwill from the new partner's capital
determine goodwill by comparing the implied capital with the actual capital
work out the goodwill inferred from the amount the incoming partner brought in

solution_steps.explain: divide what the entrant brought by his fraction to get the implied total capital
the excess of implied over actual total capital is the hidden goodwill

concepts.title: Accumulated Profits and Reserves Distribution
concepts.definition: Reserves and undistributed profits earned before admission belong to the old partners alone, so each takes his old-ratio fraction of the accumulated amount.
concepts.key_idea: The entrant must not benefit from profits earned before he joined the firm.
question_patterns: calculate each old partner's share of the general reserve on admission
how is the accumulated profit divided among the old partners
find the share of reserve transferred to a partner's capital account
what portion of the accumulated profits goes to each existing partner
distribute the general reserve between the old partners in the old ratio

solution_steps.action: apply the old fraction to the accumulated amount
solution_steps.explain: each old partner's slice of the reserves follows the old profit ratio

concepts.title: Revaluation Profit and Its Distribution
concepts.definition: Totalling every upward revision and deducting the downward ones gives the net revaluation result, which the old partners divide in the old ratio.
concepts.key_idea: Only old partners absorb revaluation effects, because the assets and liabilities existed before the admission.
question_patterns: calculate the profit or loss on revaluation of assets and liabilities
find the net gain on revaluation transferred to the old partners
what is each partner's share of the revaluation profit
determine the balance of the revaluation account at admission
compute the old partners' share after revaluing assets and reassessing liabilities

solution_steps.explain: subtract the total downward revisions from the total upward revisions

solution_steps.action: give each old partner his slice
solution_steps.explain: the net result is split in the old profit ratio

concepts.title: Proportionate Capital Adjustment
concepts.definition: If capitals must sit in the profit ratio, the entrant's payment fixes the whole-firm capital; each partner's required capital is his profit fraction of that total, and the gap against his adjusted capital is brought in or withdrawn.
concepts.key_idea: Capitals are made proportionate to the new profit sharing ratio; a positive gap brings cash in, a negative gap withdraws the excess.
question_patterns: calculate the new capital of each partner in the profit sharing proportion
find how much capital a partner must bring in or withdraw after the admission
what is the required capital of a partner when capitals follow the new ratio
determine the surplus or deficiency in a partner's capital
adjust the partners' capitals proportionate to their profit shares
compute the proportionate capital of every partner from the entrant's contribution
calculate the new capitals of all partners when capitals are adjusted in the new profit sharing ratio
find the amount a partner brings in or withdraws to make his capital proportionate to his share

solution_steps.action: gross up to the total capital
solution_steps.explain: divide the base capital by its fraction to value the whole firm's capital
multiply the total capital by this partner's profit fraction
required capital less the capital already standing gives the adjustment; a negative figure is a withdrawal

concepts.title: Share Change on Ratio Revision
concepts.definition: When existing partners reshuffle shares among themselves, each one's gain or loss equals the new fraction minus the old fraction; a negative figure marks a sacrifice.
concepts.key_idea: Whoever gains share compensates the one who gives it up, through a goodwill adjustment.
question_patterns: find which partner gains and which sacrifices when the ratio changes
calculate the change in each partner's share after the profit ratio is revised
by how much did a partner's share increase under the new arrangement
what is the gain or sacrifice of each partner on a change in the profit sharing ratio
measure the share movement when existing partners only reset their ratios

solution_steps.action: deduct the old fraction from the new fraction
solution_steps.explain: a positive result is a gain, a negative one a sacrifice
